title: Ledger and Confession
premise: When estate lawyer Sable Pemberton is called to read the will of town founder Edmund Voss, she discovers a document dated three years after his death — and then his coffin is exhumed and found empty. Following the will's strange bequests through Hollow Creek's founding families, Sable uncovers a decades-old pact: five families faked Voss's death to cover a fatal accident at the mill, each paying into a secret 'ledger' to buy the silence of the dead man's mistress. The final heir, desperate as the money runs out, has begun killing to keep the confession buried. Sable survives an attempt on her life, forces the ledger open before the town, and chooses to honor the last true bequest: giving the unmarked grave beside Voss's empty coffin a name at last.
about_author: Isandro Okonkwo is a former probate clerk who spent seven years in small-town courthouses watching families fracture over paper. He writes mysteries about the documents people leave behind and the truths they hope no one will ever read.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Sable Pemberton's POV. Called to Voss House on a rain-slicked evening, Sable reads aloud a will dated three years after Edmund Voss's documented death. The family reacts with fury and fear rather than confusion. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into dread as she realizes everyone in the room already knew something was wrong.

chapters.title: Empty Oak
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A court order she didn't request forces the exhumation; the coffin holds only stones and a woman's locket. Sheriff Dane Mercer warns her off with unusual urgency. Emotional beat: vertigo — the one certainty of death, her profession's bedrock, dissolves beneath her.

chapters.title: Five Signatures
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and archive-clerk Theo Brandt POVs. Digging through county records, they find the mill accident file sealed by all five founding families in 1961. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt tempered by Theo's quiet terror — his grandmother signed that seal.

chapters.title: The Mistress's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She tracks Voss's undocumented companion, Lena Marsh, to a nursing home; the dying woman hands over a ledger of payments spanning sixty years, entries still current. Emotional beat: grief for a life erased from every record but this one book.

chapters.title: What the Heirs Paid For
chapters.summary: Multiple POV chapter moving through the four surviving family heads, each privately confessing their version of 1961 to themselves. All agree Voss died at the mill; none agree who was holding the winch lever. Emotional beat: complicity — survival bought with a shared lie, each generation inheriting the debt.

chapters.title: A Bequest of Ashes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The second named beneficiary in the false will, old Aldous Crane, is found dead hours after signing papers with Sable — staged as a fall. In his pocket: a page torn from the ledger naming the fifth family. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve; her signature may have marked him for death.

chapters.title: Hollow Creek Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo matches the ledger's handwriting to the current Voss heir, Camille, who confronts him at the archive and nearly kills him. He escapes with proof and calls Sable from a payphone like a man in a spy film. Emotional beat: fear transformed into courage he never knew he had.

chapters.title: The Mill at Low Water
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Lured by a forged summons to the derelict mill, Sable is trapped by Camille, who confesses everything: the pact, the payments, the murders to keep the ledger closed. Emotional beat: cold clarity — Sable keeps her talking, recording, buying minutes with questions about belonging and what the town owes its dead.

chapters.title: Confession, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Climax. Sable's POV. Sheriff Mercer arrives — not to arrest Camille but to bury the case one last time — until Sable plays the recording and reads the ledger aloud to the assembled town on the courthouse steps. Emotional beat: catharsis; the price of survival finally comes due, publicly, irreversibly.

chapters.title: A Name at Last
chapters.summary: Resolution. Sable's POV. Months later, she probates a new will — her own drafting — restoring Lena Marsh's name to the Voss plot and dissolving the founding families' trust into restitution. Camille awaits trial; Theo archives the truth openly. Emotional beat: quiet belonging — Sable, an outsider, becomes the keeper of the town's honest memory.
